beats.say: A training job can gain GPUs and still take longer per update. The work has to be divided along useful boundaries, and every division introduces communication. Megatron begins with ownership: which worker computes a layer shard, which processes another sample, and which holds the next layer range?

Megatron Core supplies parallel layers, process groups, schedules and optimizer machinery. Megatron-LM provides reference training recipes around those building blocks. Megatron Bridge connects checkpoint representations and recipes across ecosystems. These projects cooperate, while their interfaces answer different implementation questions.

We will place one rank on a mesh, split a small feed-forward calculation, fill a pipeline and exchange remote attention context. Then we will connect optimizer ownership to a recoverable checkpoint. Every calculation uses small constructed inputs so the ownership changes remain visible.

A worker that cannot store one wide matrix needs a different split from a worker waiting for a hot expert. Tensor parallelism divides layer channels; pipeline parallelism divides layer ranges; context parallelism divides sequence positions. Data replicas process independent samples. Expert parallelism distributes sparse networks. Selective recomputation trades stored activations for repeated forward arithmetic.

Follow one sample through that choice. Its tensor shards cooperate inside layers, its activation crosses pipeline boundaries, and its queries may consume remote context. Data parallelism supplies other samples rather than shortening this sample’s path. Use the smallest supported combination that removes the measured wall, then inspect the new wait.

This tour anchors rank construction to the article’s August twenty twenty-six commit ending four four two two a nine six. Additional generalized-tensor weight-rematerialization factors stay one in our fixtures. That is a declared baseline, not a promise that every newer launch has the same factors. A live guide can change independently of this source.

Core owns parallel modules, process groups, schedules and distributed state. The reference trainer owns a runnable experiment’s data, tokenizer, logging and arguments. Bridge supplies conversion and training workflows. Record Core, Bridge, Transformer Engine, CUDA, NCCL and PyTorch identities together. The CPU calculations here initialize no communicator and establish no GPU throughput or convergence.

Begin with eight ranks: two tensor coordinates, two data coordinates and two pipeline coordinates. Tensor varies fastest, then data, then pipeline. Rank three is tensor one, data one, pipeline zero. Its tensor partner is two; its data partner is one; its pipeline partner is seven. Vary one coordinate while retaining the others.

For the larger dense fixture, tensor four, context two, data four and pipeline two multiply to sixty-four. The chosen strides are one, four, eight and thirty-two. A global rank equals tensor coordinate plus four times context, plus eight times data, plus thirty-two times pipeline. Logical adjacency still needs a launcher placement receipt before it implies a fast physical link.

Factor this dense world into tensor shards, pipeline stages, context lanes and data replicas. Their product assigns every rank once. In our chosen ordering, tensor coordinates change fastest. Highlight rank three and follow the nearby tensor peers that cooperate on its layer arithmetic.

Change the selected group to pipeline peers. The partner now has a distant global rank number because the pipeline coordinate changes on a larger stride. Rank numbering describes a logical layout. The launcher must still place those ranks on suitable devices and physical links.

Finally highlight the data peers. They process independent examples while holding corresponding model shards. Each operation communicates in the group that owns its data. Context parallelism adds a sequence axis; sequence parallelism reuses tensor peers for selected activation work and adds no extra world-size factor.

The numbering helper repeatedly takes the remainder by an axis size, then divides the remaining rank by that size using integer division. For rank twenty-seven, the tensor remainder is three. After division, context remainder is zero; data remainder is three; pipeline remainder is zero. Rebuilding gives three plus twenty-four, or twenty-seven.

Its tensor group is twenty-four through twenty-seven. Its pure data group is three, eleven, nineteen and twenty-seven. Its pipeline partner is fifty-nine. The pinned rank generator builds groups from these dimensions and rejects a world that does not divide by the model-parallel product. Independent batch count uses pure data replicas; dense gradient ownership can include context peers.

The article’s larger MLP uses hidden width eight, intermediate width sixteen and four tensor shards. In mathematical input-times-weight notation, each up shard is eight by four and each down shard is four by eight. The source stores linear weights as output features by input features: four by eight, then eight by four. The transpose preserves the same ownership.

The article’s standard-library tanh approximation to GeLU computes the serial eight-coordinate output, then sums four sharded partial vectors. Their maximum difference stays below ten to the minus twelve for that supplied calculation. This checks CPU decomposition with biases, dropout, sequence parallelism and backward omitted. Fused GPU kernels have their own rounding and tolerances.

Split the output channels of a feed-forward layer's first projection. Each rank receives the same input but owns different intermediate channels. Our small matrices calculate the four projected coordinates explicitly. The two highlighted groups are real channel shards, rather than independent data examples.

Apply GeLU separately to each local coordinate. An elementwise function needs no neighboring channel values, so these shards can remain local. The following projection owns matching rows. Each rank turns its local activation slice into a partial contribution to the final output vector.

Sum the partial output vectors and compare with the serial calculation. They agree within numerical precision. This column-then-row structure avoids gathering intermediate channels between the projections. Other communication appears in backward or sequence-parallel variants, and a final output bias belongs after the partial sums combine.

The forward sum is only part of training communication. In backward, each column shard contributes to the gradient of the same replicated input, so those input-gradient contributions must combine. Sequence-parallel paths can replace some replicated reductions with reduce-scatter and all-gather. Do not count the one-forward-all-reduce drawing as a full training trace.

For a bias check, supplied partial outputs are one and two, with one shared output bias of three. Sum the partials and add the bias once: six. Adding that bias on both shards before the sum gives nine. The problem is duplicated model arithmetic, even if the collective succeeds. Query-head and key/value-group divisibility also constrain attention sharding; do not assume a specialized replication path.

Pipeline parallelism divides layer depth between stages. With one microbatch, the second stage waits for the first activation, and the first later waits while the second finishes. Our forward-wave demonstration makes that startup and drain visible with equal-duration stages.

Feed several independent microbatches through the stages. Useful work overlaps across them and the ideal idle fraction falls. A real training schedule also includes backward, communication and possible stage imbalance. This simple model explains the bubble's denominator before those costs enter.

Keep the global batch fixed and double the data replicas. Each replica now receives fewer microbatches, so its pipeline fills less effectively. More GPUs can save memory yet expose a larger bubble. Count independent samples when deriving microbatches; tensor and context copies do not create extra examples.

Microbatches per replica equal global batch divided by the product of microbatch size and pure data degree. The article’s sixty-four examples, microbatch two and data degree four give eight. At sequence length two thousand forty-eight, that update contains one hundred thirty-one thousand seventy-two token positions before padding and loss masks. Tensor and context copies add no independent examples.

For equal stages and a non-interleaved idealization, idle fraction is pipeline stages minus one, divided by the quantity microbatches plus pipeline stages minus one. Bubble time relative to useful compute instead divides pipeline stages minus one by microbatches. With two stages and eight microbatches these are one ninth and one eighth. Different denominators describe the same idealized schedule.

A one-forward-one-backward training schedule also has warmup, steady state and drain. Virtual pipeline chunks can reduce bubbles but add scheduling and communication constraints. Unequal stages, message latency and insufficient compute to overlap change the result. The CPU batch helper rejects fractional microbatches; it does not simulate ramp-up or variable-length packing.

Data parallelism repeats corresponding model shards while processing independent examples. Megatron-FSDP changes ownership inside that existing domain. The named strategies shard optimizer state; then optimizer state and gradients; then optimizer state, gradients and parameters. Those choices add no new ranks to the dense world-size product.

Hierarchical optimizer instances can divide a synchronization domain into smaller sharding domains plus outer replication. A dense parameter repeated over data and context peers can therefore have a different optimizer denominator from an expert parameter. Inspect the actual parameter group, context degree and instance count before applying a memory equation. Changing ownership does not by itself prove a shorter update.

A long sequence can be partitioned across context peers. Each peer holds only some positions, but a query can still need keys from the whole legal prefix. Our equal-score query exposes the difference between using its local shard alone and using all allowed positions.

Bring the remote context into the calculation. The two partial means need weights proportional to their normalization masses. A shard's normalization mass is the sum of exponentiated scores over its allowed keys. Equal scores make those masses proportional to key counts. Subtracting the common score before exponentiating gives each key one unit of mass. The combined result matches attention over the complete seven-position prefix.

Preserve global positions and causal masking during that exchange. Actual implementations choose communication layouts and balanced chunks around the workload. Sequence parallelism has a narrower activation-memory role on tensor peers. It does not make full attention valid using only each peer's local tokens.

Sequence parallelism reuses tensor peers for selected sequence-dimension activation work such as LayerNorm and dropout. It adds no world-size factor. Context parallelism adds sequence-owning peers, while attention still consumes remote legal keys and values. Balanced implementations may assign noncontiguous chunks so that causal work is more even than a simple early-half, late-half split.

The current guide recommends sequence parallelism with tensor parallelism and requires it for the supported nontrivial tensor-plus-expert combination it describes. Context exchange can use point-to-point, all-gather, all-to-all or hierarchical layouts. An eight-thousand-token recommendation is a workload suggestion, not a minimum length for correctness. Dynamic context degrees need separate shape and performance checks.

Expert parallelism places different expert networks on different ranks. One source token can select several experts, creating several routed assignments. Follow token T-three to two experts. The system must preserve its source identity so returned vectors can be restored to the correct output position.

Apply the router weights when combining those vectors. Our unequal weights produce the calculated result below. Returning unweighted expert outputs would change the model. Route skew can also create a hot expert even when the total token count stays fixed, so inspect each expert's work.

Attention and experts can factor the same rank world differently. The two products shown here both use the same total workers. Folding can keep an expert's matrix wider while changing expert ownership. This requires compatible model shapes, routing metadata, placement and checkpoint representation rather than multiplying another expert axis into an already complete world.

Two selected experts create two assignments per token. Permutation groups those assignment rows for expert execution; combine restores each source position with its router weights. Capacity dropping may remove an overflowing assignment, while a dropless dispatcher retains uneven work. The source token can still have other selected or residual paths. Count assignments and affected tokens separately.

A hot expert is a queue even when total tokens and total assignments stay fixed. Capacity, balancing loss, grouped GEMM and overlap address different costs. Read per-expert counts alongside dispatch and combine time. A small expert divided into too many tensor shards can lose efficient matrix size while retaining collective cost; changing pipeline depth alone does not repair that imbalance.

The article’s attention grid uses tensor four, context two, data eight and pipeline four: two hundred fifty-six ranks. Its expert grid uses expert tensor one, expert sixty-four, expert data one and pipeline four: the same two hundred fifty-six. Expert data means copies of a given expert shard. It need not equal attention’s data degree.

The pinned implementation constructs separate dense and expert rank generators, with context one in the expert generator. Their pipeline groups must match. Folding can break the older expert-degree-at-most-data-degree constraint, but a correct product is only a first check. Expert count, tensor shapes, routing metadata, checkpoint keys and physical placement must also be compatible.

Computation ownership and optimizer storage are related choices. In this conventional recipe, model and gradient buffers retain six bytes per assigned parameter. Twelve further bytes belong to the master weight and Adam moments. A distributed optimizer partitions that second block across its actual sharding group.

Increase the group size and watch the optimizer-owned share shrink. Dense weights can repeat across context peers as well as data peers, so the group may be larger than the pure data degree. Activations and temporary buffers remain outside this persistent-state formula.

Reduction must also preserve the intended objective. One replica averages one valid token while another averages three. An equal average of those local means gives a different gradient from the global token mean. A correct collective and equal tensor shapes cannot detect a wrongly weighted loss.
